recipes.name: Chicken Tortilla Soup III
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup
6 boneless, chicken breast halves - cooked, skinned

steps.text: In a large pot over medium heat, saute the garlic and onion in the butter or margarine for 5 minutes. Add flour and stir well, cooking for 1 minute more. Add the broth and half-and-half. Bring to a boil and reduce heat to low.

Add the soup, salsa, corn, chicken, cumin, fajita seasoning and 2 tablespoons cilantro. Stir and continue to heat for 15 minutes. Crumble tortilla chips into individual bowls, add 1/2 ounce shredded cheese to each bowl and ladle in soup. Top each bowl with more crumbled chips, remaining 1/2 ounce cheese and remaining 1 tablespoon cilantro, and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Tortilla Soup III
raw_recipe.description: The base for this chicken stew with Mexican seasonings is made by combining chicken broth and salsa with half-and-half and condensed cream of chicken soup. Garnish with tortilla chips and grated cheese.

review.reviewBody: Fantastic Soup! I serve this in my coffeehouse and get nothing but rave reviews from my customers! I dump all of the ingredients in a crock pot in the morning, turn it to medium and it's ready by lunch. The only thing I do differently is to whisk about 1 1/2 cups flour into the chicken broth. This gives it a little thicker consistency. I also use dried onions instead of fresh and a large can of chicken (saves alot of time!). Try it, it will be one of your favorites!

This is such an easy soup and just so delicious! I followed the recipe but used an already prepared rotisserie chicken to save time. We topped it with the cheese, cilantro, green onions, a dollop of sour cream and tortilla strips- for the tortilla strips, I just cut a flour tortilla into strips with a pizza cutter and crisped them up in the air fryer. This soup recipe is definitely one of our favorites. Thank you!

not a bad base, but is overly homogeneous for me and bland if you follow it perfectly. but it is hearty and filling and very creamy which i like. my picky eaters had a problem with the texture, so i blended it with the chicken in it and it was still odd but i liked it. i halve the recipe and still end up with leftovers, i'd say it makes closer to 12 servings. i 3x the garlic, use red onion, use frozen corn instead of creamed corn because with the creamed corn it is pretty mushyand too sweet. i use my own seasoning blend over the fajita seasoning (smoked paprika, chili pwd, onion, garlic, cumin, red pepper, salt+pep, cayenne) in a higher quantity bc it's bland as-is. i add black beans, red/orange bell pepper, jalapenos+chiles. i cook the soup for 25-30 mins instead of 15 to combine flavors, and i add all the shredded cheese+cilantro in with about 10-15 min left and some sour cream a few minutes before finished. i top with extra salsa, sour cream, and i fry my own chips to which i just add to the top instead of the bottom of the bowl like the recipe suggests so theyre not mushy. with adding the solid ingredients it was a bit thick so i add more broth. i try not to have too much leftovers because it doesnt save well- the soup and dairy separate and it has a bad smell, but ends up still tasting good, for a week tops. but again, i feel like a quarter of this recipe could feed 1 for a week straight- and i doubt it would freeze well with all the dairy fat but i havent tried. i had never made soup before and this was a good starting point to get the method down but needed quite a bit of change to suit my taste.

I really loved this recipe. I made a few changes after reading some comments of it being too thin/watery. I also made mine in the crockpot for convince. In order to reduce liquid I changed the amount of chicken stock to 32oz and the amount of half and half to 2 cups. I added a small can of diced green chiles. I also omitted the creamed corn - I am just not a fan of corn. Place all of the ingredients in the crockpot except the half and half. Cook on low for 5-6hrs then remove the chicken breasts and shred them. Return chicken to the crockpot. Whisk 1/2 cup of flour into the half and half and add to crockpot. Turn heat up to high and let thicken for 1/2 hour.

This was fabulous! My husband said this was a winner! I made mine in the crock pot. I put everything in the crock pot except the half and half. (I did not use the corn to save on carbs). I cooked on high for 4 hours and then added the half and half. I cooked it for 30 more minutes and it was done and delicious!

I used 2 cans of Rotel instead of the salsa. I also used 2 pkg of fajita seasonings.

Rule of thumb my aunt taught me:
Red over white and they don't fight. Have your white base hot and cooking before pouring into the red so the white doesn't curdle. 

Great recipe! Yummy

Partner is half Mexican, & he loved it! Unfortunately, we’ve had trouble growing cilantro this year, so omitted that. Soup still turned out great. Poached the chicken in water & used that for half the broth. Subbed Mexican table cream for the half & half, & it was nice and thick. This recipe halved will make 2 meals for us. Thank you

LOVED this...couldn't get enough of it. My SO and sister were very pleased with the results! My revisions were: I did not add the corn as I'm not a big fan, I used 70 ounces of water with chicken bouillon (didn't use canned broth), and only used 2 cups of half 'n' half. Added 4 ounces of the Sargento Tastings Fiesta Jack (cut up into pieces) to add a kick and creaminess, and added a 14.5 oz can of black beans (undrained). I used dried cilantro leaves. And did NOT add any as garnish as the recipe calls for. Also, I made my own condensed cream of chicken soup (as I didn't have any on hand)--2 tbsp of butter, 3 tbsp of flour, chicken bouillon, 1/2 c. milk (1% is fine) and 1/2 c. of water), salt & pepper to taste, simmer on med-low until thick. In the end, I crushed some tortilla chips over the soup at the end. No need to add any shredded cheese or sour cream. All I know, is that this specific mix of ingredients made for an amazing soup and the household had it again for lunch the next day, and again for dinner the following night. This will be a "go-to" recipe for me and my family!

This is a good basic tortilla soup recipe. I made a few changes that made it pretty flavorful. I added two packets of sazon, an additional can of regular corn, an entire large jar of salsa (about 2 1/4 cups). I halved the amount of half-and-half. And instead of dumping in the fajita seasoning, I used the seasoning plus 1 TB olive oil, 1 TB soy sauce, 1/2 TB Liquid smoke, and 2 teaspoons lime juice as a marinade for the chicken for an hour or so. And I cooked the chicken, the onion, and the garlic with the marinade before adding it the soup.

I made a lot of changes (mostly because I didn't have what was on hand) and it came out delicious. Only had 1/2 C lt. cream so just added 2% milk to it. No salsa so I used petite diced tomatoes & a 1/2 can of green chilies. Used a Costco rotisserie chicken...so easy. Also added 1 jalapeno chopped very fine for added spice. Left of creamed corn. Everybody loved it!

This soup recipe is a keeper. I did make some changes after reading others reviews about it being bland and thin. I added about 1/3 cup of corn starch to the 1/2 & 1/2 and chicken broth before bringing to a boil. I used a packet of taco seasoning because that's what I had on hand, but also added a full recipe of taco seasoning that I found on this site. (Taco Seasoning I) Added a dash of chipotle tabasco for flavor. This all added a lot of flavor without too much heat. In addition to cream corn, I added about a cup of corn. I also added two cans of southwestern flavored white beans. I put in about 1 cup of monterey jack in with the soup. I omitted the can of cream of chicken. soup. Thick, creamy and DELICIOUS!
This is a very simple and tasty recipe!! My whole family (including an 11 and 13 yr old boy) loved it! I did add 1 can of black beans to it the 2nd time I made it. It was a great addition!
Awesome recipe! Been making for years. Family favorite .
Doubled it. Use rotiserie chicken meat from costco
I added black beans and cannellini beans for added texture and taste :)

Enjoyed the soup immensely and will make again. Used rotisserie chicken in place of chicken breast, rotel in place of salsa. I will add a little more flour the next time I cook just to make it a little thicker. Definitely a do over here!
This was bomb!! The kids already want me to make more lol
Family loved it. Love that it doesn’t take long to make. Could be adapted to slow cooker and may try that next time.
Our favorite followed to a T except for the cheese only because you cannot find a Monterey Jack in our area I use a Mexican blend? So grateful for this recipe!
